item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
531
ABPZ20 KNHC 061707
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 AM PDT Sun Sep 6 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Lowell, located several hundred miles south-southwest of Lihue,
Hawaii, on Tropical Storm Karina, located several hundred miles
east-northeast of the Hawaiian Islands, and on Hurricane Marie,
located several hundred miles west-southwest of Punta Eugenia,
Mexico.

Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
A trough of low pressure located several hundred miles
south-southwest of the coast of southwestern Mexico is producing
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Gradual development of this
system is possible, and a tropical depression could form during the
middle or latter portions of this week while the system moves
generally west-northwestward at 10 to 15 mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...50 percent.

$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Marie Public Advisory Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 061450
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Marie Advisory Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026
 
...MARIE TO CONTINUE PRODUCING DANGEROUS BEACH CONDITIONS
ALONG THE COAST OF BAJA CALIFORNIA AND SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA
FOR ANOTHER COUPLE DAYS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...23.5N 122.5W
ABOUT 800 MI...1290 KM W OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...80 MPH...130 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 9 MPH...15 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...977 MB...28.85 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Hurricane Marie was located
near latitude 23.5 North, longitude 122.5 West. Marie is moving
toward the northwest near 9 mph (15 km/h). A turn toward the west-
northwest is forecast tonight. Marie is then expected to resume a 
northwestward heading at a faster forward speed by Tuesday.
 
Maximum sustained winds have decreased to near 80 mph (130 km/h) 
with higher gusts. Steady weakening is expected to continue for the 
next several days. Marie is forecast to become a post-tropical 
remnant low on Wednesday.
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 185 miles
(295 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 977 mb (28.85 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Marie will continue to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico, the Baja California Peninsula, and
Southern California for the next few days. These swells are likely
to cause life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please
consult products from your local weather office. A depiction of rip
current risk for the United States can be found at:
hurricanes.gov/graphics_ep3.shtml?ripCurrents
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Hagen

item.title: Hurricane Marie Forecast Discussion Number 22
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026 
000
WTPZ43 KNHC 061452
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Marie Discussion Number  22
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP132026
800 AM PDT Sun Sep 06 2026

Marie has become less organized since the previous advisory and no 
longer has an eye.  In fact, the northwest quadrant is completely 
void of deep convection.  The latest subjective and objective 
satellite intensity estimates range from 59-77 kt.  The initial 
intensity is lowered to 70 kt for this advisory.

The initial motion estimate is northwestward, or 310 degrees at 8 
kt. Marie is currently feeling some pull by a mid- to upper-level 
trough currently over the U.S. west coast.  As that trough moves 
eastward on Monday and loosens its grip on Marie, the cyclone should 
turn back toward the west-northwest for a day or so.  Then, another 
mid- to upper-level low will strengthen over the Pacific to the 
northwest of Marie, causing a turn back toward the northwest, or 
possibly north-northwest on Tuesday.  The NHC track forecast is very 
similar to the previous one and closely follows the HFIP Corrected 
Consensus (HCCA) and Google DeepMind Ensemble Mean (GDMI).  Based on 
the spread in the guidance, confidence in the track forecast is near 
average.
 
Marie has already crossed the 26C isotherm, and currently resides 
within a dry, low-shear environment.  Marie will move into steadily 
decreasing water temperatures and even drier air over the next few 
days.  Around hour 48, southwesterly vertical wind shear will 
increase significantly as Marie approaches the aforementioned mid- 
to upper-level low to its northwest.  A slightly lower intensity is 
shown in the 12-36 hour time period, mainly due to the weaker 
initial intensity along with expected steady weakening over the next 
couple of days, although the NHC intensity forecast is still at the 
high end of model suite during that time.  Marie could hang on as a 
35-40 kt tropical storm in the 48 to 72 h period as the upper-level 
low may briefly provide some favorable dynamics before the shear 
becomes too strong.  The simulated satellite imagery from the GFS 
and ECMWF models suggest that Marie should lose its convection and 
become a post-tropical remnant low just beyond the hour 72 point, so 
NHC will continue to show post-tropical after that time.  After the 
system becomes post-tropical, global models show it weakening and 
dissipating in 4 to 5 days.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
